claim_boundary: Primary cryptocurrency studies provide a testable but conflicting prior for the canonical turn-of-month interval from the last calendar day through the first three calendar days. The exact spot-only long-or-cash policy may receive one preregistered historical Design/Validation test with explicit costs and no neighboring-day scan. Positive literature does not establish current OKX profitability, and failure closes this exact family without optimizing the calendar window.

fixed_mechanism.causal_hypothesis: Recurring month-boundary savings, payroll, fund-flow and portfolio-rebalancing demand may concentrate net buying pressure into a known calendar interval.
fixed_mechanism.economic_hypothesis: Holding unlevered BTC only during the canonical four-day turn-of-month interval may retain a meaningful share of passive upside with materially lower exposure and drawdown, improving fee-adjusted Calmar after two round-trip costs per month.

sources.title: Is the Turn of the Month an anomaly on which an investment strategy could be based? Evidence from BitCoin and Ethereum
sources.method_binding: Defines the dominant canonical turn-of-month interval as the last day of one month through the first three days of the next month, denoted minus one through plus three.
sources.finding: Reports that turn-of-month timing may improve return-to-risk even when it does not consistently beat buy-and-hold profit; the paper also tests optimized four-day periods, which this preregistration explicitly forbids copying or scanning.

sources.title: Turn-of-the-month effect in cryptocurrencies
sources.method_binding: Tests Bitcoin, Ethereum and Litecoin from August 2015 through August 2021 using dummy regressions and a turn-of-month trading strategy.
sources.finding: Reports positive turn-of-month returns above non-turn-of-month returns and a Bitcoin timing strategy that outperformed buy-and-hold in the studied sample.

sources.title: Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects in returns and trading volume
sources.method_binding: Studies more than fifteen million observations across seven continuously traded Bitcoin exchanges and separates return from volume seasonality.
sources.finding: Finds time-specific return anomalies but no return pattern persistent across time, while lower weekend volume is more persistent.

admission.reason: The exact feature is calendar-known before decision, the canonical rule is available in a public readable primary manuscript, the free sealed H1 path and passive comparator already exist, and the conflicting primary evidence makes the mechanism directly falsifiable without another discovery task.

uncertainty: The cited positive studies use different venues, samples and execution assumptions from the sealed OKX H1 corpus.
Two supporting sources are accessible only at publisher abstract and method-summary level; they provide context, not the exact policy binding.
Calendar correlation does not prove that month-boundary flows cause Bitcoin returns or that the effect survived after 2021.
Historical Design and Validation cannot serve as independent post-selection OOS.
